## Individual

| Category | Needs Improvement | Satisfactory |
|----------|----------------|--------------|

| Observed | Did not document observations, or observations incorrect | Documented correct observations based on analysis |

### __q1__ Planning a study (TEAMWORK)

```{r}
n_houses <- 833 # Total number of houses
n_sample <- 25  # Desired sample size

set.seed(90)   # Set a seed for reproducibility

df_numbers_random <- 
  tibble(
    house = sample(
        1:n_houses,     # All integers from 1 to n_houses
        n_sample,       # Size of our sample
        replace = FALSE # Sample *WITHOUT* replacement
      )
  ) %>% 
  # Arrange for our data collection convenience
  arrange(house)

df_numbers_random %>%
```

#### Population

Two different cities on two different islands where we survied 25 houses from each city. 
  - All of the Islanders? Only the residents of Helvig? Participants meeting certain criteria (in which case, you need to list *covariates*)?

#### Quantity of interest

Our quantity of interest is how tired the villagers are on a scale from 1 to 10. 

#### Covariates

- Villagers must be over the age of 5 and concent to the study. 
- Age of the person
#### Observation or experiment?

The Islands allows you to ask islanders to complete tasks. If you just take measurements on your participants, then it's an *observational study*. But if you also introduce something that's meant to change the outcome of a measurement (e.g., drinking coffee before taking a test), that's called an *experimental study*. You need to decide whether your study is observational or experimental.

- This is an observational study were we ask how many mintutes of vigerous physical activity per week and how tired the villager is on a scale from one to ten. 

#### Question / Hypothesis

- How is the amount of vigorous physical activity done per week in
minutes related to the amount of tiredness that a villager feels on a
scale of 1 to 10?

#### Sampling plan
- We will start by writing down the number of houses in both Mahuti and Vardo. At the time data collection Mahuti had 863 houses and Vardo had 833 houses. 
- We will start by randomly generating a list of 25 houses in each city to collect data from. 
- For each houses number generated, every member of the household over the age of five will be asked to consent to the study.
